the boot option that redfish added is inside the boot object and allows a specific boot option to be displayed and possibly enabled it disabled in addition to selected for next boot.

as pointed out in discord we already have other boot seetings modeled 


starting from the webui-vue I located the Boot object in a CV computer system which bmcweb shows are interfaces located in the xyz.ipenbmc_oroject.Control.Boot namespace.

please move these interfaces to that portion of our model.


further reflection of the BIOSConfig name space shows it's to implement the BIOS settings interface which has a separate schema and is disjoint from the boot object.



https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0268_2024.4.html#computersystem-1231

why should this be under bios settings? those are to have a definite registry object, whereas an arbitrary number of efi Boot targets can be created by any os running.

The thought process of adding this under bios was the boot option information is obtained by bios over various interface when BMC-BIOS communicates.
Thanks for pointing about the interface

The thought process of adding this under bios was the boot option information is obtained by bios over various interface when BMC-BIOS communicates. 
Thanks for pointing about the interface

Currently the interfaces are under phosphor-settings-manager. Adding the proposed interface along the same might not be good idea as it would not help us to manage the life cycle of the object well.
Bios can dynamically send the Boot option information(after each boot the information might change), bmc will have to add/remove dbus objects. Adding these interfaces with phosphor-settings-manager wont help us

aplease don't mark resolved unless you make changes to change the patch to address the comment.


I was not arguing it should be under phosphor settings manager.   I was simply stating it doesn't belong under the same interface as BIOS settings manager.   

The reason it doesn't belong there is because you can not define a finite set of settings by knowing the BIOS version.  The BIOS Configuration Manager state deals with this interface.   ain the reddish forum they have talked about the settings should be in a registry or similar.

This interface is interacting with UEFI defined variables that must be obtained before they can be set by the redfish client.

You also didn't respond to my suggestion to place these under Control.Boit with the other controls for the same redfish object.

Thanks a lot for taking your time and reviewing my patch-set. 
Sorry for marking comments as resolved. 

BIOS-BMC communication for managing settings is currently implemented in bios-settings-manager. Since boot option information comes from bios I placed these interfaces under bios config manager.

Yes, UEFI settings must be obtained from BIOS before we modify them. 
The UEFI settings can be obtained by ipmi-oem, pldm, redfish host interface. 

Currently these interfaces(from the patchset) provides the way to view CurrentBootOrder and also provides user to change the BootOrder. The user can patch under /Bios/Settings to change the Bios boot order. The backend will have to store Current and Pending Boot Order persistently. 

I feel adding these changes as part of bios-settings-manager would be appropriate as backend code can be implemented in bios-settings-manager. 
But, if adding the dbus-interfaces to Control.Boot and implementing backend logic in bios-setings-manager is acceptable I can go with that approach.

Please share your thoughts.

The issue with ipmi currently is:
1) ipmi only allows the user to select boot option such as HTTP, CD, Drive. 
There is no way currently from ipmi to select any particular drive. 
2) ipmi doesn't show information about the boot option such as Boot Option Name, Description, UEFI Path.

We have 2 interfaces here:
1) BootOrder
2) BootOptions

We can have multiple BootOption. 
BIOS will send us the multiple BootOption
For each BootOptions we create a dbus object path. 
The method to create boot option is defined in BootOrder interface
